answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. Accounts that behave honestly recover the stake; accounts caught double-claiming or colluding lose it, with penalties shared among the agents that verified the evidence. This makes a Sybil farm costly: every extra identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture, while creating identities alone earns nothing. Like a jetty supporting a voyage through karst waters, the stake anchors participation, though it cannot stop an attacker willing to burn enough capital.
